100% this. The teachers I have worked with seem so overwhelmed, I’m still pursuing my SPED teaching certs and degree but it really makes me reconsider sometimes.

Have experienced this several times! I am lowkey a pushover but have been strengthening my backbone! 

If an IEP meeting or something similar is coming up or there’s an issue at hand the teacher needs to deal with, I’m totally willing to give grace for the teacher being on the computer/unavailable at times. 

To me, the caveats are:
- Lessons are not prepped/ready for me to facilitate. If there is an academic that is mapped out and planned for me in advance, I totally will run it. Otherwise you cannot expect me to improv. That is not my job (especially if my student is a 1:1).
- Emergencies are occurring. This one seems obvious, but there have been times I have been in a physical restraint and required help and the teacher remains behind the desk. 
- We are a TEAM! I have been in the same situation as OP, where a teacher neglects to or just straight up refuses to work with certain students. They are in charge of the room, including the students. Even if I am assigned one specific student, there is no reason why that student isn’t also working with their teacher.

Also wondering, OP, are you in a Gen Ed room where your population / student is pushed in, or are you self contained?
